{{short description|American chemist}}
'''Thomas R. Cundari''' is [[Regents’ Professor|regents professor]] of chemistry at the [[University of North Texas]] and co-director of the [[Center for Advanced Scientific Computing and Modeling]] (CASCaM).

== Career ==

Dr. Cundari received his [[Bachelor of Science|B.S.]] in 1986 from [[Pace University]] in New York City and his Ph.D. in 1990 from the [[University of Florida]]. From 1990–1991 he was a postdoctoral fellow at [[North Dakota State University]]. After serving 11&nbsp;years on the faculty at the [[University of Memphis]],<ref>{{cite journal|doi=10.1007/BF01113243|title=A comparative study of the bonding in heteroatom analogues of benzene|year=1992|last1=Matsunaga|first1=Nikita|last2=Cundari|first2=Thomas R.|last3=Schmidt|first3=Michael W.|last4=Gordon|first4=Mark S.|journal=Theoretica Chimica Acta|volume=83|issue=1–2|pages=57–68|s2cid=93269697}}  Footnote on his name is a joke reference to [[Clambake]].</ref><ref>[https://www.chem.unt.edu/faculty/cundari.htm Cundari page] {{Webarchive|url=https://archive.today/20020919115057/https://www.chem.unt.edu/faculty/cundari.htm |date=2002-09-19 }}</ref><ref>[https://www.chem.unt.edu/research/computational_chemistry.html Research page] {{Webarchive|url=https://archive.today/20120730055412/https://www.chem.unt.edu/research/computational_chemistry.html |date=2012-07-30 }}</ref> Dr. Cundari joined the UNT faculty in Fall, 2002.

Dr. Cundari is one of two [[Coeditor|co-editors]] of ''[[Reviews in Computational Chemistry]]'', the foremost [[monograph]] series in the field. He is on the editorial board of ''[[Journal of Molecular Structure: THEOCHEM]]''.

Tom Cundari was chosen to participate in one of the 46 funded [[Energy Frontier Research Center|Energy Frontier Research Centers]] (EFRCs). The project is led by long-time Cundari Group collaborator, Prof. [[T. Brent Gunnoe]] (chemistry, University of Virginia). The UNT team will work with leading researchers from the [[University of Virginia]], [[Yale University]], [[Princeton University]], [[the California Institute of Technology]], [[University of North Carolina-Chapel Hill]], [[the Scripps Research Institute]], [[Brigham Young University]], [[Colorado School of Mines]], and [[the University of Maryland]] to identify novel catalysts for meeting the U.S.'s energy needs.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://cascam.unt.edu/|title=The Center for Advanced Scientific Computing and Modeling|publisher=}}</ref> The UNT team along with groups at BYU and Caltech will provide the lead in [[modeling and simulation]] research within this EFRC, entitled "Center for Catalytic Hydrocarbon Functionalization".<ref>[http://www.er.doe.gov/bes/EFRC_Synopses.pdf DOE Page about it] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090726055447/http://www.er.doe.gov/bes/EFRC_Synopses.pdf |date=2009-07-26 }}</ref><ref>[http://www.er.doe.gov/bes/EFRC_Award_List.pdf Awards] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090731170908/http://www.er.doe.gov/bes/EFRC_Award_List.pdf |date=2009-07-31 }}</ref>
